whatItIs.text: A Mediterranean mint-family herb of tiny, resinous leaves — the workhorse of bouquet garni and herbes de Provence.

historyNote.text: Thyme's history is heavier than its leaves: Egyptians used common thyme in embalming, the Greeks burned it as temple incense believing it a source of courage, Romans spread it across Europe, and medieval women gave knights thyme tokens — it also keeps its flavour dried better than most herbs.

howToChoose.text: Choose sprigs with springy grey-green leaves and a strong scent when bruised; dried thyme should smell sharply of thymol, not dust.

storage.text: Fresh thyme keeps about a week refrigerated, and freezes well for months; dried keeps sealed and dark.

useItUp.text: Whole sprigs infuse roasts, stocks, and honey; the last of a bunch dries on a windowsill in days and still seasons stews all winter.

substitutions.note: different but familiar; more Mediterranean lift
